  "per_column": [
    {
      "name": "cabin_crew_service_quality",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.9,
      "source_groundedness": 0.6,
      "hallucination_observed": true,
      "rationale": "Crew warmth/rudeness is a core 'advantage attribute' axis for high-rated airlines and is not captured by any original numeric column, so it gives strong grouping leverage. Groundedness is only moderate: sample 2 ('seats dreadful', entertainment) never mentions cabin crew, yet the column asserts 'poor_or_rude' -- a sentiment-bleed inference from the overall negative tone rather than a reading of the text. Positive samples (welcoming crew -> warm_attentive) are well grounded."
    },
    {
      "name": "service_attentiveness",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.75,
      "source_groundedness": 0.6,
      "hallucination_observed": true,
      "rationale": "Frequency/proactiveness of service is a distinct axis from crew warmth (sample 4 'crew came round regularly' -> proactive_frequent is a clean read), so it is useful, though it partly overlaps conceptually with cabin_crew_service_quality. Sample 2 has no service description yet is labelled 'minimal_or_infrequent', showing the same sentiment-driven fill on silent rows."
    },
    {
      "name": "personalized_service_mention",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.6,
      "source_groundedness": 0.85,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "A bare boolean flag with a heavily skewed distribution (7283 false), which limits analytical leverage, but it does isolate a meaningful advantage attribute (personal touches). Well grounded: sample 1's birthday-cake gesture -> True; the silent rows correctly resolve to False."
    },
    {
      "name": "ground_service_quality",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.85,
      "source_groundedness": 0.55,
      "hallucination_observed": true,
      "rationale": "Ground/airport service is a genuinely separate advantage axis absent from the original columns. But groundedness is weak: samples 1 and 3 describe only onboard experience yet are labelled 'efficient_helpful', an invented specific where the text is silent. It does correctly use Unknown/NULL for other silent rows, which is proper behaviour."
    },
    {
      "name": "food_quality",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.6,
      "source_groundedness": 0.65,
      "hallucination_observed": true,
      "rationale": "Largely a text-derived restatement of the existing 'Food & Beverages' rating, reducing added leverage, though the categorical labels add some nuance. Positive food mentions map correctly (delicious/plentiful -> excellent), but sample 2 mentions no food at all yet is labelled 'poor', again a sentiment-bleed hallucination."
    },
    {
      "name": "amenity_provision",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.7,
      "source_groundedness": 0.55,
      "hallucination_observed": true,
      "rationale": "Amenity breadth is a reasonable advantage axis not directly in the originals. However the values look heavily defaulted ('standard'/'minimal') and poorly tied to text: sample 4's abundant snacks/meals is only 'standard', and sample 2 with no amenity mention is 'minimal'. Values appear driven by overall tone more than explicit amenity evidence."
    },
    {
      "name": "seat_comfort_quality",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.6,
      "source_groundedness": 0.8,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "Substantially overlaps the original numeric 'Seat Comfort' column, capping its usefulness, but the categorical form is a fair proxy. Well grounded across samples: 'legroom spacious' -> spacious_comfortable, 'far too narrow, poor padding' -> cramped_uncomfortable, silent rows -> NULL."
    },
    {
      "name": "seat_configuration_privacy",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.5,
      "source_groundedness": 0.4,
      "hallucination_observed": true,
      "rationale": "Could differentiate premium-cabin products, but the value is near-constant ('low_privacy' dominates) and mostly unsupported: only sample 4 ('3-3-3 configuration') justifies low_privacy; samples 1,2,3,5 say nothing about seat configuration yet are all forced to 'low_privacy', an invented default rather than a source reading."
    },
    {
      "name": "customer_service_responsiveness",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.55,
      "source_groundedness": 0.7,
      "hallucination_observed": false,
      "rationale": "Complaint-handling responsiveness is conceptually distinct but overlaps heavily with cabin_crew_service_quality and service_attentiveness, limiting new leverage. In the samples it correctly returns 'not_applicable' where no complaint interaction is described; the large 'unresponsive_or_dismissive' bucket cannot be verified from samples but the shown behaviour is sound."
    },
    {
      "name": "value_for_money_perception",
      "analytical_usefulness": 0.55,
      "source_groundedness": 0.6,
      "hallucination_observed": true,
      "rationale": "Closely duplicates the original 'Value For Money' rating, so limited new axis. None of the sampled reviews explicitly discuss price/value, yet each is confidently assigned excellent_value or poor_value purely from overall sentiment (e.g. sample 2), an inference the source text does not directly support."
    }
  ],
  "analytical_usefulness": 0.68,
  "source_groundedness": 0.6,
  "rationale": "As a set, the columns supply several genuine advantage-attribute axes relevant to the query (cabin crew quality, service attentiveness, ground service, personalized service, amenities) that are not present in the original numeric ratings and would meaningfully support grouping high- vs low-rated airlines. Usefulness is dragged down by (a) partial redundancy with existing original columns for food_quality, seat_comfort_quality, and value_for_money_perception, and (b) a near-constant, largely defaulted seat_configuration_privacy. The dominant groundedness concern is a systematic 'sentiment-bleed' pattern: on rows where an aspect is not mentioned, the operator fills in a value matching the review's overall tone (poor_or_rude, poor food, minimal amenities on the negative sample; efficient ground service, excellent value on positive samples) rather than returning unknown. This produces confident specifics the text does not support and lowers groundedness for most affected columns, even though several columns do correctly emit Unknown/NULL for silent rows."
}
